Interceptor is a Chrome extension; it only runs where a real, logged-in Chrome
is. The Linux workstation has **no Chrome and no interceptor binary** — do not
try to install or run it locally there. Instead, drive the interceptor that
already lives on the Mac (where Nick stays logged into Seek, LinkedIn, etc.)
over SSH. The Mac is reachable as the `mac` / `nicholass-macbook-pro` SSH alias.

Prefix every interceptor command with the SSH hop and the Homebrew PATH (the
non-interactive SSH shell does not inherit `/opt/homebrew/bin`):

```bash
# Preflight: confirm the Mac, daemon, and Chrome are all up
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor status; pgrep -lf "Google Chrome" | head -1'

# Any interceptor command, run on the Mac's real browser:
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor open "https://www.seek.com.au/my-activity/saved-jobs" --text-only'
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor scroll bottom; interceptor wait 1500; interceptor text | tail -90'
```

Wrap long output in `| head`/`| tail` to keep it bounded. Use `timeout 90 ssh …`
so a hung page can't stall the turn. Everything else in this skill works
unchanged once you've prefixed the SSH hop — refs, compound commands, network
log, scene graph all behave identically; they just execute on the Mac.

### Bridge — macOS Native Helper App

The bridge is an optional Swift helper that runs as a LaunchAgent and unlocks
capabilities the Chrome extension can't provide on its own: OS-level synthetic
input (`act --os`), accessibility tree of native macOS apps, app control,
clipboard, screen capture beyond Chrome, audio/speech, files, notifications,
HealthKit, Apple Intelligence. ~95% of typical work doesn't need it.

**Status check:** `interceptor status` reports `bridge: running` with PID + socket
when it's up, or `bridge: not running` when it isn't.

**Lifecycle (install / verify / troubleshoot / uninstall) lives entirely in
`Workflows/Update.md` section 6.** Future updates flow through the Update
workflow — never reach for the upstream `install-bridge.sh` directly; that
script breaks on Apple Silicon (`/usr/local/bin` needs sudo, but sudoing the
whole script makes `launchctl bootstrap` target uid 0 instead of the user).
The skill's procedure is the canonical one.

**Security model — read before installing:**

- Transport is a **UNIX domain socket** at `/tmp/interceptor-bridge.sock`.
  Local-only; no network listener; not reachable from another machine.
- **No authentication on the socket.** Any local process running as your user
  can connect and execute every bridge action — including synthetic input,
  clipboard read, audio capture, screenshots. macOS TCC permissions
  (Accessibility, Input Monitoring, Screen Recording, Microphone) are granted
  to the bridge once and inherited by every socket client.
- **Marginal risk is supply-chain:** a malicious package installed via
  bun/brew/npm gains a one-step path to OS-level input/screen/clipboard without
  needing its own permission grants — the bridge has them.
- Single-user Mac threat model: acceptable, since anything running as you can
  already do this with effort. Multi-user Macs need socket hardening (see
  Update.md section 6c).
- Binary built locally from `~/Projects/interceptor/interceptor-bridge/Sources/`,

While troubleshooting an Interceptor "no extensions connected" error (2026-07-15), I repeatedly `pkill -x "Google Chrome"` on the Mac and relaunched with different profiles. Nick was actively using Chrome and interrupted: "Your work is interrupting my chrome work instead of using the interceptor."

**Why:** The Mac's Chrome is Nick's live, logged-in working browser. Killing it destroys his open tabs/work mid-session. It is attributable, shared state — not my sandbox. (Same spirit as [[feedback-outbound-explicit-approval]]: everything in that browser is his.)

**How to apply:** Never `pkill`/restart Chrome or change its profiles on the Mac. If Interceptor can't see a window or extension: (1) try `interceptor tab new <url>` and re-check, (2) wait and retry — the extension reconnects lazily, (3) if still stuck, report the blocker to Nick and ask him to click/open something — he is often AT the machine. Work in one dedicated tab (`tab new`), keep focus-stealing minimal, close only that tab when done. The Interceptor extension lives in Chrome profile "Profile 3" (Outlook - Personal Work).

# Alibaba sample enquiry — XINYI canopy accessories

Drafted 2026-09-16 for Nick to paste into the Alibaba "Contact supplier" / chat window. Not sent.

Fill the bracketed measurements before sending. The supplier cannot confirm fit from a canopy brand name alone, and the Ironman site does not publish internal dimensions, so measure the canopy (or ask Ironman for the drawing) and paste the numbers in.

## Products referenced

| # | Product | Alibaba ID | Ask |
|---|---------|------------|-----|
| 1 | XINYI Ute Canopy Accessories Kitchen Box | 1601901999935 | 1 sample, small size |
| 2 | XINYI Professional Factory Pickup Truck Canopy (kitchen unit) | 1601948665486 | Preferred over #1 if it fits the same canopy |
| 3 | XINYI Truck Canopy Wireless Electronic Lock | 1601912825742 | 1 sample set, must integrate with vehicle central locking |
| 4 | Customize Aluminum Lockable Car Roof Crossbars | 1601894330307 | 1 pair, 55 mm height |

## Vehicle and canopy facts to quote

- 2026 BYD Shark 6 Performance, dual cab, Australian delivered
- Canopy: Ironman 4x4 Raid aluminium canopy, Premium Pack (glass side panels), SKU AIM24SK06-G, 65 kg, incorporated roof rails, central-locking ready. Ironman sells a separate central locking kit (AIM24SK06-CLK) so the canopy's lock actuator wiring is designed to be tied into the vehicle.

---

## Enquiry text (paste from here)

Subject: Sample request for BYD Shark 6 canopy fitout: kitchen box, wireless lock, roof crossbars

Hi XINYI team,

I am fitting out a 2026 BYD Shark 6 Performance dual cab in Australia with an Ironman 4x4 Raid aluminium canopy (Premium Pack, glass side panels, incorporated roof rails, central-locking ready). I would like to order samples of four of your products for this build, with a view to a larger order if they fit well. Details below.

**1. Kitchen box, small size (product 1601901999935)**

Please quote one sample of the small size. I believe the small size suits my canopy. To confirm, my canopy's internal measurements are:

- Internal width between side walls at floor level: [xxxx] mm
- Internal length, front wall to rear door: [xxxx] mm
- Internal height, floor to roof: [xxxx] mm
- Side door aperture, width x height: [xxxx] x [xxxx] mm

Please confirm the external dimensions and weight of the small kitchen box and that it will pass through that side door aperture.

**2. Kitchen unit (product 1601948665486)**

This is my preferred unit if it fits the same canopy. Please tell me:

- Its external dimensions and weight for the size that matches my canopy above
- Whether it mounts the same way as the kitchen box in item 1 (floor mounted, wall mounted, or slide rail)
- If it fits, I would take a sample of this unit instead of item 1. If it does not fit, I will take item 1 only. Please advise which applies.

**3. Wireless electronic canopy lock (product 1601912825742)**

Please quote one full sample set (actuators, controller, remote and wiring). Before I order, I need written confirmation on the following:

- Can the lock be triggered by the vehicle's own central locking, so the canopy locks and unlocks with the car's key fob and door locks? If yes, please describe how it connects (for example, a 12 V lock/unlock pulse from the vehicle's door lock circuit, a CAN bus module, or a relay wired to the tailgate lock signal).
- If it only works from its own remote, please say so clearly.
- Operating voltage, standby current draw and the number of actuators in one set (I need the two side doors and the rear door covered).
- Whether it has been fitted to a BYD Shark 6 before, and if so which canopy.

**4. Aluminium lockable roof crossbars, 55 mm height (product 1601894330307)**

Please quote one pair at 55 mm height. Please confirm:

- Available bar lengths, and the recommended length for a canopy roof of [xxxx] mm external width
- That the mounting feet suit the canopy's integrated roof rails (I can send photos of the rail profile if you need them)
- Load rating, and whether the lock uses one key across both bars

**For all four items, please provide:**

- Sample price per item and any tooling or customisation charge
- Shipping cost and estimated transit time to [Melbourne / Brisbane], Australia, quoted DDP if possible, otherwise DAP with the courier named
- Lead time to dispatch
- Dimensioned drawings or spec sheets so I can check fit before you ship
- Your MOQ and unit pricing for a follow-on order of 5 to 10 sets, so I can plan the next step

I would prefer to pay through Alibaba Trade Assurance. Happy to send canopy photos and the rail profile if that helps you confirm fitment.

Thanks,
Nick Wood
[phone or WhatsApp if you want to share it]

---

## Before you send

1. Measure the canopy internals and roof width, replace every `[xxxx]`.
2. Pick the delivery city.
3. Decide whether to name a follow-on quantity at all. Naming 5 to 10 sets usually gets a better sample price and faster replies, but only say it if it is plausible.
4. Take photos of the roof rail profile and the side door aperture; the supplier will ask for them.
